data.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE REMEDIATION before this ticket's first plan review, found by reading all three remaining S-stories' criteria as the reviewer will.

THE GOOD NEWS FIRST: this ticket and its siblings eb6e and 8625 are in far better shape than the hardening tickets were. file_impact is set on all three, and most criteria are already correctly [operator-attested] — appropriate, because a parity corpus, a live vote and a denied-access drill are all observations rather than repository artifacts. Only ONE genuine defect across the three.

THE DEFECT — AC4, 'the epic ticket's text reflects that decision'. Two problems compounded:
 1. A ticket FIELD is not a repository file, and the completion verifier reads repository files ONLY. Untagged, this criterion could never be confirmed and would burn a close cycle — the same trap that has now appeared on 7cbe, b300, b5fe and 5e75. Now tagged.
 2. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST, and is why this needed prose rather than just a tag. Editing epic 061c's DESCRIPTION is a MATERIAL edit to the epic, which invalidates its plan-review attestation as stale-material. The epic closes LAST, after every child — so an edit made at the point this AC naturally gets satisfied would force a fresh review of the epic's very large plan at the worst possible moment in the sequence. The AC now says: make that edit BEFORE the epic's final review, or record the decision as a COMMENT on the epic instead, since comments are not material and carry the same information.

Sibling scan for the same class: eb6e's six criteria are five-tagged plus one in-repo (the runbook entry under infra/runbooks/, verifiable); 8625's four are two-tagged plus two in-repo (the ADR's existence and the tier-guarantee prose). Neither has an untagged out-of-repo criterion, and neither edits another ticket's fields. No further action on those two.
